item.title: Jack’s Old-Time Jam — Wed Oct 28, 5:00 PM — Jack Of The Wood
item.description:
Grab some dinner and a pint while enjoying our long-running Old-Time Jam! Featuring many talented musicians from the local WNC area, our traditional Appalachian mountain music jam runs from 5-9pm every Wednesday night at Jack of the Wood! Jack Of The Wood is still a downtown hot spot for food, brews and drink since 1997 and founders Joan and Joe Eckert who still own it, have maintained the original lively English and Irish vibe. The old-time mountain and Irish music jams continue, including a hot bluegrass jam Thursdays and brunch every Sunday. The venue extends a welcoming feeling to regulars and newcomers to this day. https://jackofthewood.com/
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Jam > Grass > Jam: The Saylor Brothers w/sg Tim Marsh & Phil Barker (7pm start tonight) — Wed Oct 28, 7:00 PM — French Broad River Brewery
item.description:
The Saylor Brothers are a jamgrass fusion group from Asheville, fronted by brothers Will & Ben Saylor, of Brushfire Stankgrass. This project is a foray further into the realm of bluegrass jam, with more emphasis on improvisation piled on top of a structure of traditional bluegrass and innovative original songwriting. As a trio with Greg Stiglets on bass, the band packs a large sound coming from three acoustic instruments, and often adds a fourth player for further improvisational and bluegrass firepower.
Jam > Grass > Jam is not an open bluegrass jam but is a residency featuring a rotating casts of special guests from Asheville’s bluegrass/jamband scene.
French Broad River Brewery is more than just a place to enjoy a drink—it’s a community hub where great beer, delicious pizza, live music, and good times come together. item.title: Swing Asheville Live w/ Blue Nickels — Wed Oct 28, 7:00 PM — Banks Ave
item.description: The Blue Nickels jazz band plays a mix of “traditional jazz”, and danceable selections from 1920s and 30s and and 40s. The band’s sensibilities reflect a love for moderate tempo, melodic, yet groovy energies. The horns tend towards counterpoint and harmonic partnership, as opposed to a “hot” or “in your face” aesthetics. Based in Asheville, the band is led by Ben Lieb, who was a founding member of a long-time Asheville favorite dance band the Low-Down Sires. He also played with Blue Marmalade, a band with some members of the Sires that formed briefly after the pandemic. Ben has a long history of involvement with Swing Asheville, and has taught Lindy Hop and Balboa off and on over the last 20 years. His longest continuous stint was with his former dance partner Eva Millwood where they taught together every Tuesday for 4 years. He is an occasional DJ for dances, former president of Swing Asheville, and used to maintain the Swing Asheville website.Joining Ben will be Bob Snope, Albi Podri

Crokinole Tuesdays at Highland Brewing Taproom Join us every Tuesday in the Taproom for an evening of flicks, strategy, and friendly competition! We’re hosting the Asheville Crokinole Club—a community of players who love this classic dexterity board game. Never played? No problem! Crokinole is easy to learn and endlessly fun. Players take turns flicking wooden discs across a circular board, aiming for the high-scoring center zones. The twist? If your opponent has discs on the board, you must hit one—miss, and your piece is out! Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just curious, come grab a pint, meet new friends, and test your skills.

item.title: WNC Sierra Club 11/4: The Conservation Power of Art — Wed Nov 4, 7:00 PM
item.description:
WNC Sierra Club Mark your calendars for our Nov. 4 program about the conservation power of art, featuring local artist Spencer Beals and Doc Varn of Preserving a Picturesque America.
**Spencer Beals** is an Asheville-based artist and community organizer. He has been making art in the River Arts District full-time for the last four years despite losing his life’s work in Hurricane Helene. He continues to host Sketchbook Club, Nature Journaling Club and conservation based art and storytelling events.
**Doc Varn** will talk about his work with the nonprofit Preserving a Picturesque America (PAPA) to continue the tradition of using the power of the arts to preserve and conserve across the country. He will share stories and visuals of how they find the exact locations where artists of the 1800s created the art that inspired the creation of state and national parks across America. item.description:
You're invited to a special evening at Little Jumbo called Conversations About Inspiration on November 11th from 6:30 - 8:30 pm.
This project is born out of my long-time marriage to musician and composer, Alan Hall. I'm fascinated and mystified that his artistic inspiration comes in the form of sound and rhythm. As a wordsmith, mine is sparked by words.
This contrast led me to wonder about how artists from all different disciplines transform inspiration into art. Are there common threads between, say, a sculptor and a composer? What about a dancer and an abstract painter?

item.title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown — Tue Nov 17, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina ***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****
**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.
Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

item.description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism Silencing the inner critic with Modern Buddhism Teacher Kadam Sharon Lovich
Most of us carry a voice that second-guesses, criticizes and quietly undermines — not just how we see ourselves, but how we see everyone around us. It picks at faults, sets impossible expectations and convinces us we're not enough. Left unchecked, that voice doesn't just damage our confidence — it sabotages our happiness, our relationships and our ability to grow. item.title: Gaming Night @ Noble Cider — Tue Jan 5, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks Roll the dice and pour a glass! 🎲🍎
Gaming Night is back at Noble Cider! Join us every other Tuesday for a night of tabletop tactics, card-shuffling chaos, and great company. Whether you’re a seasoned strategist or you still think a "meeple" is a type of small fruit, you’re welcome at our table.
### The Lowdown:
* **No Experience? No Problem:** We’re all about community. We’ll help you learn the ropes of a new game or cheer you on while you figure it out. * **The Library:** We have a solid stash of games ready to play—from quick party favorites to deeper strategy titles. * **Bring Your Favorites:** Have a game gathering dust on your shelf? Bring it along! We love seeing what the community is playing. * **The Vibe:** High-quality cider, cozy atmosphere, and just the right amount of competitive spirit.
**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**
Source: Asheville's Bored Game Geeks

item.title: Come sing with us! Vocal workshop and rehearsal - Land Of The Sky Chorus — Tue Jan 5, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Asheville Area A Cappella Singers Whether you are an experienced singer, or just like to sing in your car, come join us as our guest! The Land of The Sky Chorus, located in Asheville, NC, is welcoming guests - men and women - who are interested in joining us in the world-wide community of a cappella singing.
No experience is required; we provide music, voice training and an enjoyable singing experience under expert leadership. Our repertoire of music is fun and spans many styles - most songs are easy to learn and sing. Learning materials are provided to help you get started, and you will be paired with a singing "Buddy" so you can join in right away.
We will be here to greet you as early as 6:15pm to help you get situated.
Source: Asheville Area A Cappella Singers
